a3793.speaker: Joy Basu, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of African Affairs for Economic and Regional Affairs
a3793.speech: Said she was happy to see that American taxpayers' money, through the energy transformers installed under the second MCC compact, has served to improve the lives of the Beninese people.

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: Said the journey "hasn't been easy as a foreign affairs minister when you attend a lot of international meetings"; noted the country is a member of SADC, SACU, the African Union, the Commonwealth, the Organisation for African Caribbean and Pacific States and the United Nations: "It's an immense and technical task which requires vigilance." ; "When you are foreign minister, you are the face of your country internationally, meaning wherever I am, our flag is hoisted. Thus I need to, wherever, give our foreign policy position. It wasn't easy, especially since we are novices in governance. My duty is to transform this ministry for the benefit of Basotho."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On advice from his predecessors: "Yes, I have had the honour to meet with them. As a governance practitioner, I know that I need to ask those with experience...I have spoken to 'Matsepo Ramakoae and Monyane Moleleki. I also had meetings with those who served as ambassadors and with the ministry's staff in a bid to understand how things operate." ; Said one of his first engagements was to meet ambassadors from different countries and development partners stationed in the country to get a feel of the challenges they experience ; On frequent changes of ministers: "I personally believe it doesn't help us at all. Every there is a change of government starts matters anew."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On speculation that Prime Minister Ntsokoane Matekane wanted to move him to the Ministry of Energy: "(Laughing) I don't know the prime minister's thoughts. I will only know them when he has communicated with me saying 'Man move from here to there.' It's just a rumour. My vision and what I know is that for the CEO and management to make worthwhile progress, they need to be given time. I am not an advocate of too many changes."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On establishing a professional foreign service: "We are lucky that this is contained in the Tenth Amendment to the Constitution for it to be part of the law. From there we want to establish the Lesotho Institute of Diplomacy, an organisation of diplomats which will include people who have been to foreign missions and those working in the ministry as well as students with an intention of becoming diplomats. We will accept them all in the body." ; "Our mission will lead foreign policy and technical support on how issues need to be handled. They write research papers and then advise the ministry. From there we need to collaborate with NUL (National University of Lesotho) to establish a Centre for Diplomacy where diplomats will be trained. Our staff should also be trained, in other countries there are certificates for international relations offered."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: Responding to criticism that he is hiring unqualified people to head foreign missions: "It's not true! If you have time to assess our database for people in foreign missions, two of them were previously directors at foreign affairs. It says they are experts. Others have worked outside the country. Indeed, people have to be politically aligned to serve the mandate of the government of the day." ; "We come from a time where positions were created for people's qualifications to suit vacancies... It's the past governments that used to delegate those types of individuals."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On summoning ambassadors and high commissioners for a briefing: "Those consultations need to happen frequently. The world is dynamic; hence, we needed to call them in in a bid to give them a new mandate... The last time we had one such gathering was in 2017." ; Said unemployment is really bad, crime is skyrocketing and corruption is high, and that a diagnosis of these issues points to low productivity and too many imports eroding the country's money ; "As a government, we summoned them (high commissioners) to inform them that our focus is to improve agriculture. We want to build agriculture aggregation centres in communities just like you have with wool and mohair. We have also asked to find us technical and institutional support for the agriculture ministry." ; Said another mandate is a focus on the energy sector, generating electricity from solar, water and wind: "It's a good mix of renewable energy." ; "Lesotho has mountains and valleys, we need to attract tourists. You will remember we have offered a visa-free stay for European Union countries. When they land here, they are bringing in money. Hospitality is a huge sector which can grow the economy."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On the argument that the visa exemption should be reciprocal: "We have started negotiations for us to also be exempted. We need to agree that Lesotho needs those countries more than us. For it is to attract those people to come here, that is why we have taken the first step. If we were to enter into those negotiations, we would take five years without reaching an agreement."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On replacing diplomatic heads whose contracts are ending: "We have started that process of recruiting new ones, making a valuation of qualifications and ultimately appointing those who are fit. Hiring an ambassador is a political deployment; we cannot just open it saying 'we are hiring.' There's no country where that happens, you will know in the future when we have replaced them; then you can make your own assessment."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On why the ambassadors' meetings had to be face-to-face rather than virtual: "Giving a mandate is very difficult, it requires us as government, the ambassadors, the ministries, the prime minister and the King Letsie III to meet. Most times we do hold virtual meetings. But on this issue of taking the mandate, we saw it fit to engage face-to-face. In a virtual meeting, an individual can just put on the device and carry on with other business. Ambassadors had to be here so they can understand exactly our standpoint as a government. If we make an analysis of costs, we see it proper."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On accusations that Prime Minister Matekane intends to deploy the army to Goma, DRC: "The issue of deploying the army there hasn't been discussed. SADC is the one that deploys, not Lesotho. We worked together to man the head office in Goma. However, those who sent soldiers - our country wasn't part. We will not deploy them without SADC, we are part of the region, we can't just wake up one day and send the army to another country."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On allegations that the prime minister has mining interests in the DRC: "Let us throw that matter away. There's no truth to that; he doesn't have an interest in those mines. Furthermore, there's nowhere he can deploy our army to protect his personal interests."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On moves in Zambia and Zimbabwe to amend constitutions to extend presidential terms: "We support countries that align with their constitutions because if it doesn't happen one is likely to start wars in those states. We are saying to those leaders 'If the constitution says they should take two terms, that is what they should do.' But if there are amendments, citizens will state how this should happen. We would like for them to protect their countries and uphold democracy as per their respective constitutions."

a3835.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Foreign Affairs Minister
a3835.speech: On criticism of how he engages with South Africa at the recent binational meeting: "A binational commission (BNC) is the highest relationship in international affairs where the heads of governments meet at least once a year together with ministers, where relations between the two are reviewed. Our relationship with South Africa (SA) is kind of a special one since we are completely surrounded by them." ; "That BNC is more fruitful for us than SA. That is why you will notice that for a meeting to take place, we as the government, initiate it. If it doesn't happen, Basotho will suffer. We are in the process of signing a BNC with Botswana, we have started negotiations with them." ; "If you check, there were some cases of xenophobia in SA; all those attacks against Basotho didn't succeed. Why do you think they fail? That is because where they are planned, there's a Mosotho who says 'This issue of making my people suffer will not happen.'"

a3989.speaker: Perfectual Linnan Labik, communications professional, social entrepreneur and gender advocate
a3989.speech: Believes that one can be a slay queen and also a successful boss in her field ; said in an interview with The Mirror that she enjoyed looking good and is often described as a “slay queen” ; said that people were often surprised and confused when they saw her as the organiser of conferences and a leader in her industry ; “For me, it's always the expression of shock and confusion on their faces because I love to dress well and look fabulous. I enjoy life and many people see me as a slay queen, as the term is used in Ghana” ; explained that those who initially looked down on her believed she was a woman without ambition ; “Many people are quick to judge based on appearance, but I believe an industrious woman can also look good. A woman can be versatile in her looks and still excel in her field. My life is a testament to the idea that women shouldn't feel constrained. Women must be assertive because you can achieve anything while looking great.”

a3989.speaker: Perfectual Linnan Labik, communications professional, social entrepreneur and gender advocate (on her career journey)
a3989.speech: Noted that many who encountered her were surprised when they compared her appearance with her accomplishments, having initiated the Northern Education Support Initiative between 2012 and 2017 right after high school ; noted that her experiences as a social entrepreneur and communications professional helped her transition into the corporate world ; “During the interview, when I was asked about my job experience, I shared details about the projects I had undertaken through the Northern Education Support Initiative. I received the job offer and worked there from 2019 to 2021” ; “Looking back, I realised how significant it was because I was very young. Just imagine the Ghana Education Service (GES) entrusting students to my care, transporting them to various locations in the region and ensuring they received meals. I managed this for five years before I was selected for the internship” ; “Two months later, I was informed that I would be taking on the role of communications lead, marking the beginning of my career in communications” ; noted that many of her supervisors commented that her contributions far exceeded those expected.

a4085.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Ahoussinou, 2nd Deputy Mayor of Porto-Novo
a4085.speech: In his address, said that this project has come at just the right time and will enable women in remote areas to be informed of the realities. He urged participants to reflect deeply so that this phenomenon can be brought under control in the two departments and in Porto-Novo.

a4409.speaker: Faras Raad, World Bank country manager for Malawi
a4409.speech: Says Malawi’s economic development has evolved slowly and yielded modest improvements in living standards; said since independence in 1964, GDP per capita has risen from about $197 in 1965 to $394 in 2021, averaging under 1.5 percent growth per year; said there were periods of high growth from 1964 to 1979 and from 2006 to 2011, but significant setbacks in the 1980s to 1990s, after 2012, and during Covid-19, with climate shocks causing damages of roughly 1.5 to 2.7 percent of GDP ; “As a result, extreme poverty has remained stubbornly high: over 75 percent of the population live under the international poverty line of $3 (about K5 000) per day. Against this historical development backdrop, current macroeconomic challenges also abound, per capita growth in 2024 was negative for a fourth consecutive year, the country’s fiscal deficit is one of the highest on the continent, inflation remains significantly elevated, the parallel forex premium exceeds 100 percent and official forex reserves are at about two weeks of import cover.”

a4409.speaker: Faras Raad, World Bank country manager for Malawi
a4409.speech: Said the bank is hoping for the reform agenda to pick up following the election, and that “the World Bank stands to support any reform agendas to make sure that macroeconomic stability is restored”.

a4409.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Scotland-based Malawian economist
a4409.speech: Earlier attributed the country’s stagnation to internal structural and governance issues ; “Externally, global economic shifts and trade dynamics pose both risks and opportunities. Leveraging Malawi’s position within regional trade blocs such as the African Continental Free Trade Area could unlock new markets for Malawian products.”

a4409.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Malawian Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a4409.speech: Said the new National Social Protection Policy is a collective promise to shift from emergency relief to long-term resilience, inclusive development and building a fairer society.

a4458.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4458.speech: Says the US attack on Iranian nuclear facilities in Fordo, Natanz, in Isfahan Province, and Esfahan city brought together the warring parties to a ceasefire agreement; in a post on Truth Social said both Iran and Israel came to him simultaneously for a truce: “Ceasefire!” I knew the time was now,” he wrote. “The world, and the Middle East, are the real winners. Both nations will see tremendous love, peace, and prosperity in their futures.” ; stated that both countries have “so much to gain,” but also “so much to lose” should they stray from the “road of righteousness and truth” ; declared that the ceasefire between Israel and Iran is now in effect and urged both parties to stick with the agreement ; declared that the ceasefire would take effect after 6 hours, with the Iran ceasefire beginning at 04:00 GMT and Israel following 12 hours later at 16:00 GMT, the window giving both sides time to complete their “final missions.”

a4458.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4458.speech: Is believed to have told the Qatari ruler: “I’ve got the Israelis, but we need the Iranians on side.”

a4458.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4458.speech: Said the Iranian attack on American bases in Qatar and Iraq was largely symbolic, and noted that the strikes were intercepted as Iran had informed it beforehand.

a4458.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4458.speech: Described the 22 June strike as a “successful attack” and said: “We have completed our very successful attack on the three Nuclear sites in Iran, including Fordow, Natanz, and Esfahan. All planes are now outside of Iran’s airspace.”

a4458.speaker: Al Jazeera (report)
a4458.speech: Reported that the White House believes negotiations began between Mr Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and that after securing Israel’s agreement to halt its strikes, the president turned his attention to Iran.

a4458.speaker: Local Iranian media outlet (reported via Al Jazeera)
a4458.speech: Reported that Mr Trump called Iranian officials, pleading for a ceasefire.

a4458.speaker: CNN (report)
a4458.speech: Reported that President Trump communicated directly with Mr Netanyahu, while Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff negotiated terms with Iran through direct and indirect channels.

a4458.speaker: Israeli government (statement issued Tuesday morning)
a4458.speech: Said it has achieved its goals, saying the Iranian nuclear facilities have been destroyed and no longer pose an existential threat to the country; the prime minister, his cabinet, the minister of defence and the head of the Mossad met “to report that Israel had achieved all of the objectives of Operation Rising Lion, and much more.” “Israel has removed a dual immediate existential threat – both in the nuclear and ballistic missile fields” ; “The Israeli military achieved full air control over Tehran’s skies, inflicted severe damage on the military leadership, and destroyed dozens of central Iranian government targets. In light of the achievement of the operation’s objectives, and in full coordination with President Trump, Israel has agreed to the president’s proposal for a bilateral ceasefire.”

a4458.speaker: US intelligence sources (told the Washington Post)
a4458.speech: Said that Iran had moved its enriched uranium and other critical equipment from the nuclear facilities before the US bombing.

a4458.speaker: IAEA, the UN atomic agency
a4458.speech: Acknowledged that the US bombings damaged the three Iranian nuclear facilities but that the extent of the damage could not be established yet.

a4458.speaker: Iran (government)
a4458.speech: Said it will halt attacks if Israel stops its “illegal aggression” ; justified its attack on American bases in Qatar and Iraq by describing it as an act of self-defence, and a “clear and explicit” message to the White House.

a4458.speaker: Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s Foreign Minister
a4458.speech: Said in a post on X: “As of now, there is NO “agreement” on any ceasefire or cessation of military operations. However, provided that the Israeli regime stops its illegal aggression against the Iranian people no later than 4 am Tehran time, we have no intention to continue our response afterwards.”

a4458.speaker: Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s Foreign Minister
a4458.speech: Praised the Iranian military, saying: “Together with all Iranians, I thank our brave Armed Forces who remain ready to defend our dear country until their last drop of blood, and who responded to any attack by the enemy until the very last minute.”

a4458.speaker: Israel (government)
a4458.speech: Described the 13 June attack on Tehran as a preemptive strike to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons, and said Iran’s nuclear development programme posed a threat to its national security.

a4458.speaker: Iran (official casualty report)
a4458.speech: Reported that more than 400 people have been killed and over 3,056 others injured.

a4600.speaker: Sam Kawale, Malawi Minister of Agriculture
a4600.speech: Has underscored the pivotal role of agriculture in generating foreign exchange for Malawi, stating that the government is committed to supporting agricultural activities nationwide to achieve the country's Vision 2063 ; highlighted the importance of moving from subsistence farming to commercial practices ; emphasized that the government's efforts, including the recent purchase of a K56 million advanced rice processing machine funded by the Agricultural Commercialisation (AGCOM) Project, are aimed at enhancing productivity ; “This machine will process 20 tonnes of rice daily, helping us move towards having locally produced products on the shelves and eventually exporting them, which is crucial for forex generation.”

a4600.speaker: Sam Kawale, Malawi Minister of Agriculture
a4600.speech: Acknowledged the challenges posed by the need for electricity to run the processing machine, revealing that discussions with the Ministry of Energy are underway to address this issue ; assured that electricity for agricultural activities will be subsidized, and solar equipment will be imported duty-free to support energy access in the sector.

a4600.speaker: Sam Kawale, Malawi Minister of Agriculture
a4600.speech: Highlighted the importance of research in fostering a vibrant agricultural sector; acknowledged challenges such as encroachment on land and understaffing at the Lunyagwa Agricultural Research Station, asserting that investment in research is essential for increasing productivity ; “Research is fundamental. We need to identify which crops thrive under specific conditions and how to optimize inputs for better yields,” emphasizing a collaborative approach with surrounding communities to address encroachment issues and enhance agricultural outputs.

a4600.speaker: Robins Ndawa, Chairperson of the Nkondezi Cooperative
a4600.speech: Expressed gratitude for the new equipment, stating it will help produce quality rice that meets market standards ; “This equipment will remove dust and residues from our rice, allowing us to meet the Malawi Bureau of Standards' requirements.”

a4713.speaker: Tione Chilambe, National Aids Commission (NAC) official
a4713.speech: Said Malawi in its sustainability plan had expected donor support to reduce over time, but not as quickly as it has, especially around HIV prevention services: "We knew the money would eventually reduce, but not in such a sudden way."

a4713.speaker: Tione Chilambe, National Aids Commission (NAC) official
a4713.speech: Said that to keep services running the government responded by allocating K1 billion towards HIV treatment co-financing and setting aside K0.5 billion to hire and train more health workers.

a4713.speaker: Unaids
a4713.speech: Has warned that if the funding gap is not filled, there could be an additional six million HIV infections and four million Aids-related deaths globally by 2029.

a4713.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Unaids Executive Director
a4713.speech: "We cannot let funding cuts wipe out the gains we've made."

a4713.speaker: Musa Manganye, head of HIV treatment in South Africa
a4713.speech: Said what matters is the budget line.

a4729.speaker: Arnold Robinson, Quincy Jones' publicist
a4729.speech: Said he "passed away peacefully" on Sunday night at his home in Bel Air.

a4729.speaker: Time magazine
a4729.speech: Named him as one of the most influential jazz musicians of the 20th century.

a5077.speaker: Walinase Msiska, cross-border trader from Chitipa District
a5077.speech: Admits she has been running the business without export permits, hence the use of uncharted routes ; "It is very risky, sometimes we lose it all when we are caught by Police who patrol these routes regularly together with MRA [Malawi Revenue Authority]."

a5077.speaker: Steve Yohane, President of the Crossborder Traders Association (CBTA)
a5077.speech: Confirms that cross-border trading has a myriad of challenges that put off potential traders while pushing many into smuggling, many of them involving processes of obtaining various permits ; "We have been engaging authorities to iron out issues cross border traders face every day but not much is changing."

a5077.speaker: Project brief on the National Single Window facility (document)
a5077.speech: "Single Window solution is a one-stop platform for information exchange between traders and government agencies involved in international trade, integrating customs, ports, maritime authority and other government agencies through electronic ICT platform." ; "The NSW is a highly convenient tool for private sector stakeholders since all information associated with trade or related transport transactions is submitted and retrieved from a single system. Private sector stakeholders reap the benefits of electronic access: savings in time and resources since physical submission and collection of documents are eliminated." ; further explains that border control agencies are linked to the NSW platform to process transactions but operate in the background, with workflow management of their organizations integrated into the NSW.

a5077.speaker: Christina Chatima, Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Trade
a5077.speech: Said cross-border traders from all corners of the country will be able to apply and obtain permits online once the national single window is operational.

a5128.speaker: Trans Murder Monitoring project (report)
a5128.speech: Reported that 375 murders between October 1, 2020, and September 30, 2021, a 7% increase from the previous year, which was already a 6% increase from the 2019 figure... A total of 4,042 trans and gender-diverse people (LGBTQ+) were reported murdered from 2008 through September 30, 2021.

a5128.speaker: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR)
a5128.speech: Documented 770 killings and seriously violent attacks against LGBT persons between January 1, 2013, and March 31, 2014, including 594 hate-related killings of LGBTI people in Brazil. The IACHR cited reports indicating that every 28 hours an LGBT person is violently attacked in Brazil.

a5128.speaker: Grupo Gay da Bahia (report)
a5128.speech: Found that Brazil's number of reported deaths rose in 2017 to a record level of 435, a rate of one LGBT person killed every 19 hours.

a5128.speaker: Silueta X Association, Ecuadorian LGBT+ rights group (report)
a5128.speech: Reported that in Ecuador in 2019, 16 LGBT+ people were murdered or suffered violent deaths.

a5128.speaker: FBI
a5128.speech: According to the FBI, in the United States, out of the almost 6,000 gay murders committed in 2013, 20% (approximately 1,200) were based on victims' sexual orientation.

a5128.speaker: National Coalition of Anti-Violence Programs
a5128.speech: Reported an increase of 86% in the hate-based murders of LGBTQ people comparing 2017 and 2016, even excluding the 49 murders in the Pulse nightclub shooting of June 2016.

a5128.speaker: Alimshaikh Aliev, father of Raina Aliev
a5128.speech: Called for his daughter's execution on a Russian TV station, referring to Raina Aliev as “him”: “Let him be killed, I don't want to see him. Bring him here and kill him in front of my eyes.”

a5128.speaker: Yishai Schlissel, convicted murderer of Shira Banki
a5128.speech: Claimed that his murderous violence was designed to fulfill the imagined “obligation of every Jew to keep his soul from punishment and stop this giant desecration of God's name.”

a5128.speaker: The Advocate
a5128.speech: Reported, “The artistic freshman had faced incessant bullying at Horlick High School, family and friends told Racine's Journal Times.”

a5128.speaker: Jamie Olender, mother of Cameron Langrell
a5128.speech: According to her mother she “apparently faced much teasing for appearing 'feminine'”; Jamie Olender called for schools to provide bullying prevention, because lives are at stake.

a5128.speaker: LGBT community members in Turkey
a5128.speech: Accuse police of failing to conduct a serious investigation of the November 17 murder of a 27-year-old man from Antakya, Turkey, identified as F. I.; they believe his murder was a homophobic crime. They said F. I. was last seen heading out for a rendezvous with a Syrian man, and that the police joked about F. I.'s text messages and released the three men without recording their names.

a5128.speaker: Pedro Araujo (online post)
a5128.speech: Hours before he was killed, Pedro Araujo protested online against violence and attacks on homosexuals. He posted three photos of young people who had been beaten and commented, “These young people were beaten just for being gay. Say no to homophobia.”

a5128.speaker: Mauritanian law (Penal Code, 1984; Article 308)
a5128.speech: “Any adult Muslim man who commits an indecent act or an act against nature with an individual of his sex will face the penalty of death by public stoning.”

a5128.speaker: The Bible (Romans 1:32; Leviticus 18:22; Leviticus 20:13)
a5128.speech: “Although they know God's righteous decree that those who do such things deserve death, they not only continue to do these very things but also approve of those who practice them” ; “You shall not lie with a male as with a woman; it is an abomination” ; “If a man lies with a male as with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination; they shall surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.”

a5128.speaker: Peter Sprigg
a5128.speech: Identifies the following effects of gay marriages: Taxpayers, consumers, and businesses would be forced to subsidize homosexual relationships; Schools would teach that homosexual relationships are identical to heterosexual ones; Freedom of conscience and religious liberty would be threatened; Fewer people would marry; Fewer people would remain monogamous and sexually faithful; Fewer people would remain married for a lifetime; Fewer children would be raised by a married mother and father; More children would grow up fatherless; Birth rates would fall; and Demands for legalization of polygamy would grow.

a5128.speaker: TFP Student Action (statement of 5 February 2015)
a5128.speech: Stated reasons why gay marriages are harmful and should not be legalized, noting ten points: It Is Not Marriage; It Violates Natural Law; It Always Denies a Child Either a Father or a Mother; It Validates and Promotes the Homosexual Lifestyle; It Turns a Moral Wrong into a Civil Right; It Does Not Create a Family but a Naturally Sterile Union; It Defeats the State's Purpose of Benefiting Marriage; It Imposes Its Acceptance on All Society; It Is the Cutting Edge of the Sexual Revolution; It Offends God.

a5146.speaker: Save the Children
a5146.speech: announced a new Grants-under-Grant program in which the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Growth Through Nutrition Project will provide more than nine million Ethiopian birr (more than USD 300,000) to three woredas in support of the Government of Ethiopia’s Seqota Declaration to end child under-nutrition by 2030; over the next year, the grants will support Debark and Ebinat woredas in Amhara regional state, and Nader Adet woreda in Tigray, by strengthening the woreda authorities’ capacity to deliver locally appropriate nutrition interventions.

a5161.speaker: Kutluhan Yucel, Coordinator of the Turkish Cooperation and Development Agency (TIKA) in Djibouti
a5161.speech: Indicated during an address delivered on this occasion that the pastry sector is developing in Djibouti and that his organisation had supported CASAF with equipment and expertise. “We provided, on the one hand, household appliances and kitchen utensils and, on the other hand, we made available to the centre a chef of Turkish gastronomy to deliver intensive courses on pastry-making.”

a5161.speaker: Selim Levent Şahinkaya, Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a5161.speech: Revisited the partnership between the CASAF centre and TIKA, which in his view has made it possible to strengthen the technical capacities of this centre for the empowerment of Djiboutian women.

a5161.speaker: Neima Yonis Hoch, Director of CASAF
a5161.speech: “Our primary objective is to fight illiteracy and poverty. It is in this sense that we give women and girls here training in promising trades with a view to empowering them economically,” in her words of welcome.

a5161.speaker: Mouna Osman Aden, Minister of Women and Family of Djibouti
a5161.speech: Declared that her department wishes to reorient CASAF’s mission “to facilitate the full inclusion of young girls who have failed at school through the FEMFI programme, which plans, after carrying out an assessment of vocational training needs, to put in place other, more technical trainings that match the needs of the market.”

a5161.speaker: Mouna Osman Aden, Minister of Women and Family of Djibouti
a5161.speech: Addressing the Ambassador of Turkey, she indicated that “the forms of partnership between the CASAF centre and TIKA make it possible to strengthen the relations between our two countries but even more to more easily integrate our young girls and women in general into the labour market.”

a5161.speaker: Mouna Osman Aden, Minister of Women and Family of Djibouti (interview, ‘A word with…’)
a5161.speech: “The Centre for Social Action and Women’s Empowerment (CASAF) is a non-profit social organisation. Operational since 2007, the Balbala Women’s Training Centre is a second-chance school… Since its creation, the centre trains 30 learners per section each year, divided into 1st and 2nd years. The trainings are divided into 3 sections: cooking, hairdressing and sewing, i.e. 180 learners… From 2017 to 2021, more than 900 girls have benefited from these various trainings offered by CASAF. Of this figure, there are 653 certified graduates, of whom 40% have been placed in the job market.” ; “The partner TIKA will always remain a partner, including the other partners such as UNDP and USAID, as relays in the programme of the Ministry of Women and Family (MFF), which is to develop and implement the Government’s policy on the social and professional integration of vulnerable women (notably those operating in the informal sector).”

a5226.speaker: Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and AIDS Affairs of Tanzania (report)
a5226.speech: said that a large share of the implementation of HIV and AIDS interventions in the country depends on donor funds from outside Tanzania, the absence of which could slow the pace of the fight against the epidemic.

a5226.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a5226.speech: announced the suspension of new funding and of disbursements under Development Objective Agreements (DOAGs) until the review of USAID-funded country assistance programmes is completed; the review is expected to be completed within 85 days starting from January 24, 2025.

a5226.speaker: Elibariki Kingu, Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and AIDS Affairs
a5226.speech: said that a large share of the implementation of HIV and AIDS interventions in the country depends on donor funds from outside the country: “If that funding comes to an end, it could to a large extent cause the country to slow the pace of the fight against that epidemic for lack of sufficient funds” ; proposed that Parliament resolve that the Government fully implement the sustainability plan for the HIV and AIDS response so as to obtain sustainable domestic resources in the fight against HIV and AIDS without depending on aid from donors.

a5226.speaker: Mussa Zungu, Deputy Speaker of the Tanzanian Parliament
a5226.speech: put the question to the MPs and they passed the resolution by a majority of voices: “Yeeees.”

a5226.speaker: Jacqueline Kainja, Special Seats MP (CCM)
a5226.speech: said the Tanzania Commission for AIDS (TACAIDS) depends to a large extent on funds from donors outside the country, particularly through the US President’s Emergency Plan (PEPFAR) and the Global Fund for AIDS, Malaria and Tuberculosis: “In the 2024/2025 budget, at the Commission for AIDS Control (TACAIDS), 86 per cent is money from outside the country, equivalent to 11.36bn/-, compared with domestic funds which are equivalent to 14 per cent, that is 1.8bn/-” ; “If we look at things now, our counterparts in America — the President has announced that he is suspending services under that emergency fund of his; we do not know how long that fund will be halted. As a nation, how are we planning?” ; asked the Government that the sustainability plan for the HIV and AIDS response, launched on December 1, 2024, continue to be supervised and to function, in order to remove uncertainty among citizens living with HIV.

a5226.speaker: United States Department of State
a5226.speech: has said that PEPFAR has been included in the waiver for life-saving humanitarian assistance during the 90-day suspension of foreign aid; among the activities permitted are care of people living with HIV, testing and counselling, prevention and treatment of tuberculosis, laboratory services, procurement and distribution of health commodities and medicines, and services to prevent mother-to-child transmission.

a5226.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5226.speech: ordered, a few hours after taking office on January 20, 2025, the suspension of foreign aid so that it could be examined to see whether it aligns with his “America First” foreign policy.

a5226.speaker: Elibariki Kingu, Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and AIDS Affairs
a5226.speech: on health insurance: said that in the 2024/25 financial year sources of funds to cover people without means under the Universal Health Insurance (UHC) Act had been identified, which were expected to collect 173.5bn/-, but the amount collected was small — only 47.13bn/- up to November 23, 2024, equivalent to 27 per cent; said the committee recommends that Parliament resolve that the Government involve private sector stakeholders in contributing to the fund; said the challenges of running the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) cause negative effects on operations, so amendments to Chapter 395 should aim to recognise the private health sector: “It should strengthen ICT systems in order to pay health service providers on time and to control fraud in the use of health insurance, and provide education to the community on the importance of health insurance services and a better lifestyle with the aim of tackling non-communicable diseases.”

a5226.speaker: Elibariki Kingu, Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and AIDS Affairs
a5226.speech: on organ transplantation: said the committee recommends that the Government complete the process of preparing a law on the harvesting, preservation and transplantation of human cells and organs, to protect human rights, ensure health safety and prevent the illegal trade in human organs: “Carrying out those services without the existence of a formal law could cause negative effects on society, including the violation of human rights and the emergence of an illegal trade in human organs.”

a5226.speaker: Fatuma Toufiq, Chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Social Welfare and Community Development
a5226.speech: said PSSSF ought to refund and claim that money from the employers as the law directs: “This act removes the employee’s confidence in that fund; it should not be tolerated by Parliament, which is the authority with law-making powers; it conflicts with the purpose for which that fund was established, of ensuring the welfare of members” ; “These retirees are forced to pay because they have nothing else to depend on other than their benefits. This matter is not right at all, especially considering that the law does not prevent a retiree from being paid his benefits even if the employer has not completed his contributions” ; said PSSSF holds retirees responsible for its own failure to enforce the law; said the Government should take swift and firm measures, including deregistering organisations involved in moral erosion contrary to the country’s cultures, in money laundering, and in politics during elections; said 937.3m/- of the Women’s Development Fund (WDF) that was lent out has not been repaid.

a5226.speaker: Mwanaidi Ali Khamis, Deputy Minister for Community Development, Gender, Women and Special Groups, and Dr Godwin Mollel, Deputy Minister for Health
a5226.speech: said the Government would work on all the arguments and resolutions issued by Parliament.

a5570.speaker: Adelino Muchanga, President of the Supreme Court of Mozambique
a5570.speech: Says there is no arrest warrant issued by any Mozambican court against presidential candidate Venancio Mondlane; adds that if Venancio returns to the country he will continue to be a free man and that the courts will not be an obstacle to peace and harmony among Mozambicans.

a5570.speaker: Management of the Chimanimani National Park in Manica
a5570.speech: Says the acts of vandalism of its offices which occurred in the early hours of Monday have nothing to do with political motivations.

a5570.speaker: Lionel Macicame, administrator of the Chimanimani conservation area
a5570.speech: Points to artisanal miners (garimpeiros) trying to discourage the actions of the rangers as the masterminds of the sabotage.

a5570.speaker: Jose Cabral, President of the Sofala Provincial Athletics Association
a5570.speech: Proposes the restructuring of the calendar of national competitions to allow clubs to prepare; said the provinces do not have tracks suitable for athletics in the rainy season.

a5570.speaker: Valige Tauabo, Governor of Cabo Delgado
a5570.speech: Urges the managers of the Provincial House of Culture to continue investing in the training of the new generation of artists, betting on talented children from various districts; he was speaking on the occasion of the twenty-eighth anniversary of the province's so-called cathedral of the arts.

a5570.speaker: Health authorities (Niassa province)
a5570.speech: Say that the two cases testing positive for cholera vibrio in the city of Lichinga are not sufficient to declare an outbreak of the disease.

a5570.speaker: Ministry of Health of Mozambique
a5570.speech: Is carrying out, from 9 to 14 December, an emergency vaccination campaign for more than two million children in order to break the chain of transmission of the measles outbreak that has caused eleven community deaths and around three hundred and thirty diagnosed cases in Nampula province.

a5851.speaker: Minority Caucus in Parliament of Ghana, led by Dr. Isaac Opoku
a5851.speech: At a news conference in Kumasi, expressed concern over the government's failure to adjust the producer price of cocoa and wondered why the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government will not increase the producer price for the 2025/2026 season.

a5851.speaker: Dr. Isaac Opoku, Member of Parliament for Offinso-South (Minority Caucus)
a5851.speech: Said the posture of the government raises a number of questions and queried why there could not be any price adjustment irrespective of what happens on the international and local markets; said it is clear the government is reneging on its campaign promise to pay the cocoa farmer 70% of the Free On Board (FOB) price, in sharp contrast to the NDC's manifesto promise (page 43) and promises to pay cocoa farmers GHC6,000 per bag; said cocoa farmers believed in these promises and voted overwhelmingly to bring the NDC into power, hence the government must stop the numerous excuses, honour its promise and increase the producer price now.

a5851.speaker: Dr. Isaac Opoku, Member of Parliament for Offinso-South (Minority Caucus)
a5851.speech: Disputing the reasons cited by COCOBOD, indicated that the producer price review committee is a standing committee already in place and that the Board of Directors of COCOBOD has no role in the formation of the committee, hence cannot be used as an excuse not to increase the producer price; disclosed that as at February 2025 cocoa purchased and taken over by COCOBOD was more than 560,000 tonnes, close to US$3 billion (GHC45 billion) based on the achieved average FOB price; argued that the government must not hide behind COCOBOD's debt to deny farmers their legitimate share of the FOB for their toil; queried, "What operational challenges are so compelling that COCOBOD cannot increase the producer price of cocoa?"

a5851.speaker: Dr. Isaac Opoku, Member of Parliament for Offinso-South (Minority Caucus)
a5851.speech: Disclosed that the recent price hike in La Cote d'Ivoire - from CFA 1,800 to CFA 2,200 per kilo, a 22.24% rise - has created a significant disparity that threatens to exacerbate cocoa smuggling across the border, with Ivorian farmers now receiving GHC3,635 per 64kg bag, GHC535 more than in Ghana, a "stark difference" that "presents an irresistible incentive" for smugglers to divert Ghanaian cocoa, particularly from Western South, Western North and Brong Ahafo; warned that cocoa farmers might tend to sell their cocoa farms for illegal mining activities, especially in the face of surging gold prices.

a5851.speaker: Dr. Isaac Opoku, Member of Parliament for Offinso-South (Minority Caucus)
a5851.speech: Called on the government to take "immediate and decisive" action to address the pressing issue, noting that the time for lamentations and blame game has passed: "This is not merely an economic decision, but a matter of national security and preservation of our agricultural heritage."

a5851.speaker: Ghana COCOBOD (two letters of April 8 and 9, 2025, signed by Dr. James Kofi Kutsoati, Acting Deputy Chief Executive, Operations and Public Affairs)
a5851.speech: Gave reasons for not increasing the producer price of cocoa; the two letters were said to have discrepancies in the reasons cited.

a5905.speaker: Rohey John Manjang, The Gambia's Minister of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources
a5905.speech: Underscored the importance of homegrown solutions, stating that Africa must be innovative in solving its own challenges: “I know, for Africa to go forward with our limited resources, we need to be innovative in making sure that we fix our problems. We cannot just say that we do not have money.” ; Described the Jospong waste management model as a proven, comprehensive African solution, adding that it eliminates the need for expensive feasibility studies promoted by Western institutions: “What we saw these past three days was amazing; it broke our hearts for the simple reason that I could not have imagined the solution that Western countries and institutions proposed—with its inherent debt—was right here with us in Africa.”

a5905.speaker: Rohey John Manjang, The Gambia's Minister of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources
a5905.speech: Stressed that governments cannot handle sanitation issues alone and must partner with the private sector: “That is why I set for myself a six-month target, up to June, to build a waste management unit with PPP for The Gambia.”

a5905.speaker: Rohey John Manjang, The Gambia's Minister of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources
a5905.speech: Acknowledged the shared environmental challenges between Ghana and The Gambia, stating that her country's reliance on Ghana's expertise was a logical and necessary step: “We have a lot in common with Ghana, and we believe that by working together, we can find solutions to our environmental challenges.”

a5905.speaker: Dr Joseph Siaw Agyepong, Executive Chairman of Jospong Group of Companies
a5905.speech: Attributed Jospong's success to strategic thinking and divine orchestration: “When ideas marry strategy, the product is money. So, money is the son of strategy and ideas. What we need in Africa is ideas and strategy, not money.”

a5905.speaker: Dr Joseph Siaw Agyepong, Executive Chairman of Jospong Group of Companies
a5905.speech: Warned against Africa's reliance on foreign aid, citing comments from former US President Donald Trump, who urged African nations to develop their own natural resources instead of depending on foreign assistance: “If over the years, we’ve been happy with grants and loans, today Donald Trump has told us that we should go and develop our minerals.” ; Noted that the continent's dependency on aid had hindered progress, urging African nations to prioritise innovation and determination: “Collective determination and commitment are what has birthed what is happening in the waste management sector of Ghana.”

a5905.speaker: Ibrahim Murtala Muhammed, Ghana's Minister of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation
a5905.speech: Urged The Gambian government to protect Ghanaian investors, citing the historical ties between Ghana and Gambia that date back to the pre-independence era: “The relationship between Ghana and Gambia predates independence. Our former Presidents, Kwame Nkrumah and Sir Dawda Jawara, were friends and comrades in the struggle for independence.”

a5905.speaker: Ibrahim Murtala Muhammed, Ghana's Minister of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation
a5905.speech: Stressed that investment thrives on security, adding that businesses will only flourish if investors feel protected: “You are not just representing Jospong Group, but Ghana. Your operations should promote Ghana, and we will ensure that you do not embarrass Ghana because the country’s image is on the line.”

a6177.speaker: Rasaque Manhique, Mayor of Maputo
a6177.speech: Familiarised himself with the operation of the station and encouraged the public television service (during a visit to the facilities of Televisao de Mocambique).

a6177.speaker: Authorities (Tete province)
a6177.speech: Call for sustainable fishing, to protect the species, and for the reporting of illegal operators at the Cahora Bassa reservoir.

a6177.speaker: Environment Sector (Zambezia Province)
a6177.speech: Listed the introduction of new export policies, the fall in the price of timber on the international market and the inoperability of the Port of Quelimane as the main causes of the yearly decline in the number of loggers interested in exploiting forest resources in Zambezia Province.

a6177.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a6177.speech: Says that the ANC is not thinking about coalitions because his party will obtain enough votes to govern alone; states that "coalitions are thought about by those who do not believe in victory."

a6499.speaker: African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) (press statement)
a6499.speech: Explains in a statement sent to the press that, in partnership with Kipay Investments SAS, the Bank will finance the technical and bankability studies, legal fees, financial advisory services and fundraising for the development of a hydroelectric reservoir project of up to 200 MW along the Lufira River, and will also play a leading role in structuring the project’s debt financing; according to the document, the project is in line with Afreximbank’s climate finance strategy and marks its first private-sector renewable energy initiative in the DRC, providing clean, reliable and affordable energy to mining companies, expanding electricity access for neighbouring communities and cutting greenhouse gas emissions by about 108,000 metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent per year.

a6499.speaker: Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice-President of Afreximbank for intra-African trade and export development
a6499.speech: “This signing ceremony underscores Afreximbank’s commitment to supporting renewable energy projects that drive industrialisation and export development activities while promoting a just energy transition. Afreximbank is committed to supporting the DRC’s energy transition, strengthening the country’s energy security while harnessing its vast renewable energy potential to develop sustainable, trade-enabling energy infrastructure” ; “This financing reinforces Afreximbank’s commitment to mobilising private capital to develop renewable energy projects and secure a sustainable future for the DRC and the region. We are also proud to highlight the innovative structure deployed, which encompasses a captive market improving the project’s bankability.”

a6499.speaker: Eric Monga, CEO of Kipay Investments SAS
a6499.speech: Emphasised that the project had generated renewed optimism for socio-economic development among the local population and across the country: “It is important that local communities enjoy the benefits of the project – including the creation of new jobs and capacity building for the future renewable energy sector in the DRC.”

a6609.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
a6609.speech: Had indicated that after signing the agreement government will wait for the funds to be released.

a6609.speaker: Lawmakers of the House of Assembly and the Senate of Eswatini
a6609.speech: Unanimously supported the loan Bill for the major national project which is expected to create up to 800 direct jobs and boost economic growth, and praised the loan, sourced from Taiwan, for strengthening longstanding diplomatic ties and aligning with His Majesty King Mswati III's vision of achieving first world status for Eswatini.

a6609.speaker: Manqoba Khumalo, Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade of Eswatini
a6609.speech: Said the industrial park represented a new chapter in Eswatini's bilateral relations with Taiwan. “We have already identified 158 hectares of land at Pocweni near the Royal Science and Technology Park for phase one, with plans to expand to 500 hectares as the project develops” ; “The establishment of this industrial park demonstrates our commitment to fostering international partnerships and creating sustainable employment opportunities for our people.”

a6663.speaker: Peter Kapala, Zambian Minister of Fisheries and Livestock
a6663.speech: Described Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) as a "significant threat to livelihoods, food security and economic development" in the southern African region, and warned that the highly contagious viral disease, which mainly affects goats and sheep, has the potential to cripple rural economies if left unchecked: "PPR is not just an animal health problem - it is a livelihood problem. Millions of our people, especially in rural communities, depend on small ruminants for income and protein. If this disease were to spread into Zambia, the consequences for food security and poverty reduction would be devastating." ; noted that Zambia's small ruminant population - estimated at 5.5 million goats and 300,000 sheep as of April 2023 - forms a critical pillar of household income for smallholder farmers and that protecting these resources was essential for the country's broader agricultural and economic resilience.

a6663.speaker: Peter Kapala, Zambian Minister of Fisheries and Livestock
a6663.speech: Said Government has been proactive in prevention, with surveillance efforts dating back to 2010, although Zambia has never recorded a clinical case of PPR: "Our surveillance systems and early warning mechanisms are in place to ensure that Zambia remains free of PPR. But we cannot do this in isolation - diseases do not respect borders. That is why this regional buffer zone is so critical."

a6663.speaker: African Union Inter-African Bureau for Animal Resources (AU-IBAR)
a6663.speech: Revealed that Africa will need EUR 528 million over the next five years to eradicate PPR, a deadly livestock disease that threatens food security and rural livelihoods across the continent; emphasised that governments must explore innovative financing models such as targeted livestock levies, public-private partnerships and pooled regional procurement to close the funding gap.

a6663.speaker: Hiver Boussini, AU-IBAR team leader for the PPR eradication and control programme
a6663.speech: Said the financing target is critical if Africa is to meet its goal of eliminating PPR by 2030: "External support is catalytic, but national ownership and domestic financing must lead. Above all, it is the sovereign responsibility of each Member State to mobilise and sustain the resources required to eradicate PPR - for the benefit of its population."

a6663.speaker: Bogdan Stefanescu, European Union team leader for social sectors and governance counsellor
a6663.speech: Said the EU has already committed EUR 8 million for the preparatory phase of the Pan-African PPR Eradication Programme and pledged an additional EUR 50 million for Phase II from 2027: "If we coordinate through SADC and other regional bodies, we can reduce costs, accelerate progress, and protect PPR-free countries while moving closer to a continent free of the disease."

a6774.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) latest El-Nino update (report)
a6774.speech: "So far, 18,500mt [metric tonnes] of maize have been distributed, in line to meet 5.7 million people affected by hunger, which represents 28 percent of Malawians affected."

a6774.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) latest El-Nino update (report)
a6774.speech: "Recent data indicates a significant increase in malnutrition cases over the past year. The number of children suffering from severe malnutrition rose by 23 percent, increasing from 3,050 cases in December 2023 to 3,762 cases in December 2024" ; indicates that at the same time, cases of moderate malnutrition surged, rising by 178 percent from 1,358 to 3,782 cases.

a6774.speaker: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma)
a6774.speech: Has sent requests to WFP to provide transport support of maize from the Strategic Grain Reserves, which the National Food Reserve Agency manages.

a6774.speaker: Kettie Mpanda, 52-year-old food aid recipient in Nsanje
a6774.speech: Told The Daily Times in Nsanje on Wednesday that her home was affected by the problem of acute shortage of food, with a cup of maize selling at K9,500 each in most of the local markets in the district: "I have been surviving through other means because food made from maize has been difficult to find. The maize market was very unpredictable, with a cup of maize fetching K9,500 in some markets. This resulted in our failure to buy maize for food. We were failing to buy maize for food because it was expensive."

a6774.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a6774.speech: Say that while resources have been mobilised, there is an urgent need to scale up humanitarian assistance, especially in delivering food assistance to those at risk of hunger.

a6774.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a6774.speech: Say poor crop yields and rising food insecurity are causing many families to struggle with feeding their children before school.

a6774.speaker: Government of Malawi (estimates)
a6774.speech: Government estimates show that El Nino has negatively impacted 44.3 percent of the national maize crop.

a6841.speaker: George Macheka, NFRA Chief Executive Officer
a6841.speech: Confirmed in an interview that the National Food Reserve Agency has imported 20,000 metric tonnes of maize from Tanzania, saying the decision comes as domestic maize prices rocketed to between K1,600 and K1,800 per kilogram; said the importation aimed to ease pressure on the local maize market, increase supply, and stabilise prices: “The additional funding we received towards the end of 2024 allowed us to import maize to support both humanitarian assistance and Admarc’s [Agricultural Development and Marketing Corporation] affordable maize sales.” ; “This intervention ensures that people affected by hunger can access free maize through Dodma [Department of Disaster Management Affairs], while Admarc sells maize at K790 per kg.”

a6841.speaker: George Macheka, NFRA Chief Executive Officer
a6841.speech: Said NFRA plans to commence maize procurement as early as April to prevent similar challenges in the upcoming season: “We are committed to ensuring that maize is available and accessible to all Malawians. Early procurement will help us secure enough stocks before prices spiral.”

a6841.speaker: Sameer Suleman, Chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Agriculture
a6841.speech: Described the situation as worrisome: “The government could have introduced deliberate laws to regulate maize prices and protect both farmers and consumers.” ; “It is disheartening that while NFRA and Admarc have no maize in stock, vendors are already dominating the market.” ; criticised the government’s failure to allocate resources to NFRA and Admarc in time, making it difficult for these institutions to compete with private buyers: “In Zambia, it is a policy that vendors are barred from buying maize from farmers until government agencies have completed their procurement. This ensures stable maize reserves and fair prices. Unfortunately, the Ministry of Agriculture here has ignored such strategies.”

a7096.speaker: IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC)
a7096.speech: Announced, after nearly two years of persistent drought conditions, that heavy rains could fall over East Africa over the next three months; its March to May 2022 forecasts show higher chances of a strong rainy season, but stakeholders must still prepare for worst-case scenarios; the southern to central parts of the region have the greatest chances of above-normal rain while western South Sudan and central and north-eastern Ethiopia are expected to receive less rain than usual ; Also estimates that high temperatures could be recorded in southern Tanzania, most of Kenya, Ethiopia, Djibouti, Eritrea and northern Sudan.

a7096.speaker: Dr Guleid Artan, Director of ICPAC
a7096.speech: Stressed in his speech that "it is very important to note that global climate models have little ability to predict the MAM season, and stakeholders must prepare for the worst. Given that we have experienced below-average rainfall over the last three seasons, a wetter-than-normal season does not mean the region will immediately recover from the effects of the drought, particularly in the eastern parts of the Horn. That is why I urge everyone to consult our weekly and monthly forecasts because they have a much higher degree of predictability."

a7096.speaker: Food Security and Nutrition Working Group, co-chaired by IGAD and FAO
a7096.speech: Estimates that 12 to 14 million people are currently in a situation of high food insecurity in Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia.

a7096.speaker: Dr Workneh Gebeyehu, Executive Secretary of IGAD
a7096.speech: Said that beyond immediate humanitarian aid, "there is an urgent need for regional and international cooperation to support national efforts aimed at strengthening the resilience of communities by investing in sustainable development as the most effective approach to managing recurrent drought".

a7096.speaker: IGAD (Intergovernmental Authority on Development)
a7096.speech: Renewed its call for an immediate scaling up of humanitarian and risk-reduction efforts, mainly by the respective national governments, humanitarian actors and development partners, and called on humanitarian actors to advocate for no-regret interventions ; Urged the governments of member states to increase investments in drought-resilience-building interventions, in particular IDDRSI, and to adopt innovative approaches to drought risk management, including forecast-based anticipatory actions.

a7126.speaker: Government of Malawi
a7126.speech: The government says it is working hard to ensure that the gap left by the aid previously provided by the United States Agency for International Development (USaid) is filled, so beneficiaries do not suffer.

a7126.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Minister of Information and government spokesperson
a7126.speech: Speaking to The Daily Times, said the government is finding ways to ensure that those who were benefiting are not suffering: "We have an obligation as a government to find ways and means of ensuring that our people do not suffer. We still need aid, yes, but Malawians can be assured that their government will find ways of serving them in the absence of aid."

a7126.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Minister of Information and government spokesperson
a7126.speech: He, however, could not disclose President Lazarus Chakwera's reaction following the departure of one of the country's top health partners.

a7126.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Minister of Information and government spokesperson
a7126.speech: "It is President Chakwera's wish to move this country from perpetually depending on donors to a fully self-sufficient economy where the suspension of aid will have a different impact."

a7126.speaker: Willy Kambwandira, Executive Director of the Centre for Social Accountability and Transparency
a7126.speech: Commenting on the impact, said the suspension of US foreign aid is a serious blow to developing countries such as Malawi: "This is a gap that cannot be filled anytime soon, and the government has not demonstrated signs of attaining economic independence." ; He further said the suspension of US aid has come at a very awkward time, when the economy and service delivery have completely collapsed.

a7126.speaker: USAID (stop-work order and award suspension notice)
a7126.speech: Last month, USaid issued a stop-work order and award suspension notice to its implementing partners in Malawi.

a7198.speaker: Dr Mohammed Ibrahim, Head of the Disaster Risk Management Unit, ECOWAS (speaking on behalf of the Director of Humanitarian Affairs, Dr Sintiki Tarfa-Ugbe)
a7198.speech: Underscored the impact of disasters on West African communities over the past 25 years, noting losses exceeding a billion dollars, and highlighted the growing frequency and intensity of disasters driven by environmental degradation, rapid urbanization, and climate change ; "Member States must prioritize humanitarian assistance and invest in resilience-building programs in collaboration with partners to mitigate these challenges."

a7198.speaker: Alhaji Idris Mohammed, Nigeria's National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) (speaking on behalf of Director General Hajiya Zubaida Umar)
a7198.speech: Emphasized the urgent need for cooperation and collaboration for effective management of disasters across the region, stating that "West Africa is increasingly vulnerable to floods, droughts, epidemics, and conflicts - events that threaten lives and reverse development gains. Now is the time to strengthen partnerships and build a resilient and united sub-region." ; "By sharing experiences, expertise, and resources, we can build a more resilient region," he added.

a7198.speaker: Alhaji Idris Mohammed, Nigeria's National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) (speaking on behalf of Director General Hajiya Zubaida Umar)
a7198.speech: Shared Nigeria's ongoing efforts to train disaster management professionals through partnerships with six federal universities, offering certificate to postgraduate programs in disaster and development studies, aimed at building regional expertise; emphasized NEMA's commitment to working with disaster management agencies of ECOWAS member states to enhance the collective capacity to prepare for and respond to disasters: "We have done it in the past, and we ready to build on our past achievements."

a7198.speaker: Major (Rtd.) Dr Joseph Bikanyi Kuyon, Chairman of GECEAO and Director General of Ghana's National Disaster Management Organization (NADMO)
a7198.speech: Commended Ghana's recent legislative reforms empowering NADMO and announced the development of a national Disaster Risk Financing Strategy; stressed the need for capacity building and called on participants to use their expertise to inform policy and drive impactful resource allocation ; "Our collaboration must translate regional hydro-meteorological warnings into tangible preparedness and mitigation actions." ; "Let us integrate disaster risk reduction into our national development plans for 2025-2026 and work toward GECEAO's vision of harmonized disaster management in West Africa."

a7203.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (official report of the session of 5 March 2025, chaired by Captain Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso)
a7203.speech: Deliberated on the matters on its agenda, heard oral communications, made appointments and authorized missions abroad.

a7203.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (deliberations under the Ministry of Economy and Finance)
a7203.speech: Adopted three reports: gave its agreement for the conclusion by direct negotiation of a contract with the consortium Conciergerie Africa Business (CAB) Sarl / Tindaogo Inter for the completion of the building housing the Bobo III Tax Centre Directorate and the Bobo Land One-Stop Shop Directorate, for 753,825,472 CFA francs over eight months; gave its agreement for direct-negotiation contracts with PRESTIGE MULTI SERVICES (944,712,695 CFA francs for rehabilitating the Hauts-Bassins Regional Treasury buildings and 203,963,251 CFA francs for the Treasury Deposit Bank counters) and with IMPACT INGENIERIE ET CONSEIL (35,899,080 and 7,650,820 CFA francs for supervision and control); and adopted an ordinance authorizing ratification of the 18 billion CFA franc loan agreement signed on 11 February 2025 with the OPEC Fund for International Development (OFID) to finance the human capital protection project, expected to deliver free consultations for 1,840,000 women and 2,070,000 children under five in 2025, 97% pentavalent vaccination coverage, certification for 98% of teachers and annual examinations for 96% of pupils.

a7203.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (deliberations under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabe Abroad)
a7203.speech: Adopted four reports: gave its agreement for the appointment of Mr Boubakar Hassan as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Niger to Burkina Faso, of Mrs Feriba Duygu Hokkaci Esirgen as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Turkiye to Burkina Faso, and of an Apostolic Nuncio to Burkina Faso, all resident in Ouagadougou; and gave its agreement for the transmission to the Transitional Legislative Assembly of the draft law approving the Treaty establishing the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), adopted on 6 July 2024 in Niamey, described as a historic strategic framework of cooperation between Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger allowing member States to intensify cooperation in the fight against terrorism and the consolidation of peace by pooling defence and security efforts.

a7203.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (deliberations under the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights)
a7203.speech: Adopted a decree amending decree n°0013/PRES/PM/MJDHRI of 23 January 2025 on remissions of sentence for 1 January 2025, after it turned out at the time of application that nine detainees were not eligible, allowing the withdrawal of nine names from the list; the list of persons concerned will be published in the Official Journal of Burkina Faso.

a7203.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (deliberations under the Ministry of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications)
a7203.speech: Adopted a decree on the conditions and modalities for granting, renewing and withdrawing technical approvals in information systems security, applying law n°014-2024 of 9 July 2024, in order to clean up the market for cybersecurity equipment and software and better protect national cyberspace, now requiring professionals to hold an approval to operate legally.

a7203.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (deliberations under the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Crafts)
a7203.speech: Adopted four reports: gave its agreement for the acquisition, for seventy million (70,000,000) USD, of the Tema Multi Purpose Terminal hydrocarbon depot in Ghana belonging to Blue Ocean Investment Limited in order to increase SONABHY's storage capacity and guarantee the country's energy security; and adopted draft decrees dissolving the Maison de l'Entreprise du Burkina Faso (MEBF) without liquidation, transferring its assets, rights and obligations to the State, re-creating it as a public professional establishment of the State, and approving its specific statutes.

a7203.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (deliberations under the Ministry of Infrastructure and Opening Up of Access)
a7203.speech: Adopted two reports validating the synoptic sheets of the Sikasso-Korhogo-Bobo-Dioulasso (SKBo) Project - about 115 km of roads, 150 km of rural tracks, four road works brigades and 51 km of railway rehabilitation, over four years, at an estimated total cost of 126.87 billion CFA francs financed by the Burkinabe State and the World Bank - and of the Project for the rehabilitation of infrastructure supporting the economy, estimated at 129.2 billion CFA francs financed by the Burkinabe State and the Islamic Development Bank, so as to initiate the process of mobilizing resources from the technical and financial partners.

a7203.speaker: Minister of State, Minister of Defence and Veterans Affairs of Burkina Faso (oral communication)
a7203.speech: Made a communication to the Council relating to the organization of the 2nd edition of the International Fair for Synergy in Safety, Defence and Security (SYSDEF) in Ouagadougou from 8 to 10 May 2025, an armament fair bringing together key decision-makers and industry leaders, placed under the very high patronage of the President of Faso, Supreme Chief of the Armed Forces, and to be marked by a day dedicated to the Confederation of Sahel States (AES).

a7203.speaker: Minister of Communication, Culture, Arts and Tourism of Burkina Faso (oral communication)
a7203.speech: Made a communication to the Council relating to the organization of the 5th edition of the "Nuit des Lompolo" on 24 October 2025 at CENASA, whose major innovations are the opening of the competitions to actors and companies from the other Alliance of Sahel States countries (Mali and Niger), the inclusion of circus and puppetry among individual prizes, and the increase in prizes awarded from 21 in 2024 to 27 in 2025, including three new AES prizes.

a7203.speaker: Minister of Sports, Youth and Employment of Burkina Faso (oral communications)
a7203.speech: Made communications to the Council on the organization of the 6th edition of the competition of the Schools for the Training of the Sporting Next Generation (EFORS), scheduled from 22 to 29 June 2025 in Ouahigouya and bringing together 26 schools from the thirteen regions of Burkina Faso, and on the competitions of the Union of School and University Sports of Burkina Faso (USSU-BF) for the 2024-2025 season, held in seven disciplines and registering the participation of 550 schools, universities and Grandes ecoles from 40 provinces, opened officially on 31 January 2025 and continuing until July 2025.

a7203.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (appointments)
a7203.speech: Made appointments to individual positions, including Mr Kassoum Coulibaly, General Officer, as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to Washington (United States of America), together with appointments in the Prime Minister's Office and the ministries of Defence, Economy and Finance, Security, Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity, Industry and Trade, Basic Education, Environment, Urban Planning and Housing, and Sports; and appointed Directors and Chairpersons to the Boards of Directors of the Armed Forces Health Insurance Fund (CAMA) and of the Company for the Management of the Railway Heritage of Burkina (SOPAFER-B).

a7203.speaker: Pingdwende Gilbert Ouedraogo, Government Spokesperson of Burkina Faso
a7203.speech: Issued and signed the report of the Council of Ministers session of 5 March 2025.

a7491.speaker: Many economic analysts
a7491.speech: Strongly criticized the leadership of President Donald Trump as reckless.

a7491.speaker: Richard Phillips, New York-based international Financial Analyst
a7491.speech: Is bold enough to say that for all of his bombast, under the leadership of President Donald Trump the United States has actually grown more and more to resemble a developing nation; to assert his claim, he outlined six epic failures. The five epic failures of the contemporary United States under the Trump regime are: out-of-control US fiscal and monetary policies; the rise of the police state; an inadequate and ineffective health care system; a rapidly degrading environment and a deteriorating infrastructure — failures which are also among the classic characteristics of a developing nation.

a7491.speaker: Richard Phillips, New York-based international Financial Analyst
a7491.speech: Outlined as the fourth failure the extraction economy of the United States; stressed that there is no longer much ambiguity in these weather patterns, nor any ambiguity in the statistics that measure them, and that they dovetail precisely with the direst of climate predictions, and yet President Donald Trump, with the full backing of the Republican Party, denies climate change and presses forward in promoting the unrestricted extraction and use of fossil fuels.

a7491.speaker: Richard Phillips, New York-based international Financial Analyst
a7491.speech: Further noted that, favouring extraction industries every step of the way, President Trump, again with the full backing of the Republican Party, has placed the country’s water systems, wetlands and wilderness areas at extreme risk, putting in place an environmental infrastructure common to developing rather than developed nations, and that this pattern of denial and deceit puts the United States on track to increase rather than reduce its dependence upon natural resource development, making the United States a target for all the corruption that extraction industries bring with them.

a7491.speaker: Richard Phillips, New York-based international Financial Analyst
a7491.speech: Enumerated as the sixth failure the shredding of democracy in the United States; according to him, it is President Donald Trump’s assault on democracy itself — the President seeks to put in place a form of government that is no longer anchored in the basic principles of democracy and has become detached from the tenets that shape duly elected governments in other developed nations.

a7491.speaker: United States National Weather Service
a7491.speech: Is currently predicting the possibility of approximately 20 named storms coming ashore in the United States this hurricane season.

a7491.speaker: George Tyler, economist and author of “What Went Wrong” and “Billionaire Democracy: The Hijacking of the American Political System”
a7491.speech: Stressed that few if any developed nations maintain above-ground power grids as the United States still does, and that the decrepit state of the US electrical grid does not even address the jumble of problems with crumbling roads, bridges, rail lines and waterways.

a7491.speaker: George Tyler, economist and author
a7491.speech: Argued that like despots in so many developing countries, President Trump governs more and more by decree in the form of executive orders, bypassing almost entirely the people’s elected representatives in the Congress, and that as the next presidential election approaches President Trump busies himself casting doubt on its legitimacy and throws up impediments within the United States Postal Service that are aimed at suppressing the vote, a tactic common in the most corrupt developing nations.

a7491.speaker: Frank Vogl, Co-founder of Transparency International and author of “Waging War on Corruption: Inside the Movement Fighting the Abuse of Power”
a7491.speech: Stated that corruption in Washington, D.C. is akin to the kinds of corruption one finds in places like Lagos or Kabul, albeit on a more sophisticated level; instead of foreign entities bribing local officials as happens in developing nations, United States companies bribe United States officials in the federal capital city, as well as state capitals.
